_comment: Reader profiles — WHO the brief is for, and therefore what the mandatory so-what answers, which sections appear, and what cadence fits. settings.json 'preset' picks one. The lens (feeds.json / clients.local.json) says WHAT to watch; the profile says HOW to read it for this audience. Generic by design: no client or company names here (public repo).

practitioner-brief.audience: analytics / measurement practitioners and their leads
practitioner-brief.so_what_question: What does this mean for how we measure, model, and run analytics — methods to adopt, skills to build, vendors to watch?
practitioner-brief.tone: Human and explanatory, like a sharp colleague walking you through it. Full sentences, gloss any jargon in plain terms on first use, land every item on a concrete move for the team (adopt / build / watch). Substance over brevity — this reader wants the why. EDIT THIS LINE to retune.
practitioner-brief.notes: The canonical format in SKILL.md. Craft altitude: the reader does the work.

leadership-radar.tone: Human but lean. Warm, plain, concrete, never abstract — but still an executive skim: 'the read' stays 1-2 sentences and the whole brief fits a quick scroll. Humanize the words, not the length. EDIT THIS LINE to retune.
leadership-radar.cadence: twice weekly (e.g. Mon/Thu) or weekly — timing leaders can react to beats depth
leadership-radar.so_what_question: What would I want to say in my next client conversation — and what should my team do or watch because of this?
sections: prose blocks for the top accounts (capped)
leadership-radar.sources: client/brand topics in clients.local.json (gitignored) with market-reaction follow-ups; skips GitHub releases/discovery entirely
leadership-radar.notes: Light reads only — leaders form their own view; deliver signal at the right moment, not essays. 'The read' is 1-2 lines max. At scale, prose_budget caps how many accounts get a block (see SKILL.md 'Leadership-radar at scale'); the rest live in the coverage table. Default 5 (~3 primary + 2 strongest context) keeps the brief skimmable — a 10-account test with budget 7 ran long, and the coverage table absorbs everyone else without losing the 'we checked all of them' guarantee. tier (primary/context) + account_scope on each client topic drive who gets prose and how reads are weighted.

both.tone: Each half keeps its own tone: leadership-radar blocks lean-but-human, practitioner blocks fuller and explanatory.
both.composition: leadership-radar client blocks first, then practitioner topic blocks; a single Bottom line spanning both; What shipped stays practitioner-only
both.cadence: weekly (the radar half may additionally run alone midweek)
